name: Vumbu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Bastin, Yvonne, André Coupez, Bernard de Halleux & Colette Nasse. 1994. Lexicostatistique appliquée à la zone B du bantu. Africana Linguistica 11: 9-12 (Persée).
sources.note: Nothing; direct download of the Persée page reports no mention of Vungu among the 1987 Gabon survey languages.

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1990. The Great *HL Split in Bantu Group B40. Pholia 5: 17-29.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Only Vungu content: yi-Sira 'probably includes as sub-dialects both yi-Varama.. and yi-Vungu, West of Mouila' (p.18); 'As regards Ngubi and yi-Vungu, I did not have enough data to be able to reach any conclusion' (p.19, on the two kinds of Type D nominals). Purely tonal.

sources.citation: Pholia 4 (1989), 'Catalogue des archives orales' (ALGAB / LUTO), p.201, section 'B 45 VUNGU'.
sources.note: Nothing. Records three anonymous Vungu oral narratives recorded in 1987 (clan migrations around Mouila, Malimba) and Nziengui Mouckagny 1987 'Contribution à l'histoire des Vungu' (history licence report); no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1987. Les classes nominales 9, 10 et 11 dans le groupe bantou B40. Pholia 2: 5-22. Lyon: CRLS, Université Lumière Lyon 2.
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative B40 noun-class/tone paper on i-sira, i-sangu, yi-punu, yi-lumbu; 0 hits for vungu/bungu/voungou and 0 hits for 'accent'.

sources.citation: Pholia vols. 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 (1987-1994), Lyon: CRLS/DDL, whole volumes a full-text search for stress/accent vungu/bungu/voungou/B403.
sources.note: No Vungu linguistic content at all (Pholia 7 lists 'Bavungu' among ethnic groups in a Libreville survey; Pholia 3 mentions 'les parlers des Bavoungou et des Bavarama' in passing).

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1984. Présentation du yi-lumbu dans ses rapports avec le yi-punu et le ci-vili à travers un conte traditionnel. Pholia 1: 7-35; plus the Pholia 1 'Index des langues' and 'Bibliographie' (DDL retyped edition).
sources.note: Nothing. Lists 'les parlers des Ba-Vungu et des Ba-Varama' in Guthrie B40 beside Sira, Sangu, Punu, Lumbu, with mutual intelligibility claimed by speakers; index entry 'givungu = dialecte punu'; bibliography cites Miganga 1981.
Nothing; stubs (Ghivungu / yi-vungu, ~5,000 speakers 2007, B.403 after Maho 2009; ISO name Vumbu, no change requests).

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Natalia Chousou-Polydouri & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Untangling the West-Coastal Bantu mess: identification, geography and phylogeny of the Bantu B50-80 languages. Africana Linguistica 25: 87-162.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Glottolog's subclassification source for vumb1238; its sample/appendix should name the Vungu lexical source used (a lead to primary data), nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Bostoen, Koen & Gilles-Maurice de Schryver. 2018. Seventeenth-century Kikongo is not the ancestor of present-day Kikongo. In Bostoen & Brinkman (eds.), The Kongo Kingdom, 60-102. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Second Glottolog classificatory source listing Vumbu; lexicostatistic only, may name the Vungu data source.

sources.citation: Bastin, Yvonne, André Coupez & Michael Mann. 1999. Continuity and divergence in the Bantu languages: perspectives from a lexicostatistic study. Annales du MRAC 162. Tervuren: MRAC.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Contains two Vungu wordlists ('Vungu 1 B47', 'Vungu 2 B47' = Vumbu [vum]); its source list would identify who collected Vungu data (possible unpublished field notes with tone marking). No stress statement expected.

sources.citation: ALGAB oral archive (LUTO / Université Lumière Lyon 2): three Vungu narratives recorded 1987 (Pholia 4, 1989, p.201, 'B 45 VUNGU', items 88-90).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only known primary Vungu recordings; if ever transcribed with tone marks they would be the nearest thing to prosodic data; not a description.

sources.citation: Miganga, M. 1981. Esquisse phonologique du givoungou de Yetsou. Mémoire de licence / MA thesis, Université Omar Bongo, Libreville.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only phonological description of Vungu that exists (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a phonology; cited in Pholia 1 bibliography); a UOB 'esquisse phonologique' normally has a section on tones and, if anything, on accent/length. Would decide the entry.
sources.venue: Mémoire de licence / MA thesis, Université Omar Bongo, Libreville

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page vumb1238 and reference records 29588 (Bastin, Coupez & Mann 1999, Continuity and divergence in the Bantu languages, MRAC: lexicostatistic lists 'Vungu 1 B47', 'Vungu 2 B47' = Vumbu [vum]), 569683 (ElCat 2022), 586272 (Pacchiarotti, Chousou-Polydouri & Bostoen 2019, Africana Linguistica), 586274/586275 (Bostoen & de Schryver 2018a, 2018b).
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Nothing; all are lexicostatistic / phylogenetic / endangerment surveys. Confirms Miganga 1981 is the sole descriptive reference (Glottolog lists 1 descriptive works).
